ar.title: عروض بلاك فرايداي 2026: أفضل صفقات بطاقات الرسوم للألعاب وسط أزمة الأسعار
ar.description: مراجعة لأبرز تخفيضات كروت الشاشة من إنفيديا وإيه إم دي وإنتل خلال موسم بلاك فرايداي، مع نصائح للاختيار الذكي في ظل ارتفاع الأسعار المستمر.
ar.deck: يقدم موسم بلاك فرايداي 2026 فرصة نادرة لاقتناء بطاقات رسوم للألعاب بأسعار مقبولة نسبياً، وسط أزمة تسعير حادة تدفعها طلبات الذكاء الاصطناعي العالمية.
summary_bullets: أسعار كروت الشاشة تواصل الارتفاع طوال 2026 بسبب طلبات الذكاء الاصطناعي، مما يجعل عروض بلاك فرايداي فرصة مهمة
بطاقات إيه إم دي Radeon RX 9000 Series وإنتل Arc Battlemage تقدم قيمة أفضل من عروض إنفيديا RTX 50 Series
أفضل الصفقات تشمل RTX 5060 و 5060 Ti و 5070، و RX 9070 GRE و 9070 XT، و Arc B570 و B580
ينصح الخبراء بمراجعة دقة الشاشة ومعدل الإطارات المستهدف ومتطلبات الطاقة وحجم العلبة قبل الشراء

sections.heading: أزمة تسعير غير مسبوقة تدفعها طلبات الذكاء الاصطناعي

paragraphs.text: تشهد سوق بطاقات الرسوم الاستهلاكية ضغطاً متواصلاً منذ بداية 2026، حيث يستمر التوسع العالمي في البنية التحتية للذكاء الاصطناعي في استنزاف مخزونات الشرائح المتطورة. وفقاً لتومز هاردوير، فإن الأسعار ارتفعت بشكل مطرد طوال العام، ويتوقع قادة الصناعة استمرار هذا الاتجاه، مما يجعل موسم بلاك فرايداي الحالي ربما آخر فرصة لشراء كرت شاشة بسعر معقول لسنوات قادمة. ويمكن الرجوع إلى Tom's Hardware للاطلاع على التفاصيل الأصلية للمصدر.

sections.heading: عروض إنفيديا: سلسلة RTX 50 Series تتصدر المشهد

paragraphs.text: تتنوع صفقات إنفيديا بين الخيارات الاقتصادية والمتوسطة والعالية. يبرز كرت RTX 5060 كأفضل خيار لألعاب 1080p بكفاءة عالية ودعم كامل لتقنيات DLSS 4.5، بينما يوفر RTX 5060 Ti بذاكرة 8 جيجابايت أداءً أقوى بدولارات قليلة إضافية. في فئة 1440p، يقدم RTX 5070 ثلاثي المراوح قيمة ممتازة مع دعم DLSS و Multi Frame Generation، فيما يعد RTX 5070 Ti الخيار الأمثل للمتحمسين. أما كرت RTX 5090 الرائد فلا توجد عليه "عروض" حقيقية، حيث يباع بأكثر من ثلاثة أضعاف السعر الرسمي، إلا أن بعض الطرازات تأتي مع لوحة أم مجانية كحافز إضافي. ويمكن الرجوع إلى Terms & Conditions للاطلاع على التفاصيل الأصلية للمصدر.

sections.heading: إيه إم دي وإنتل: قيمة أفضل في الفئات المتوسطة

paragraphs.text: تتفوق بطاقات الفريق الأحمر والأزرق في نسبة السعر إلى الأداء حالياً. يقدم كرت Radeon RX 9070 GRE أداءً قوياً في 1080p و 1440p بسعر منافس، بينما يرتقي RX 9070 بذاكرة 16 جيجابايت لتمكين ألعاب 4K مع التقنيات الفائقة. في القمة، يتوفر RX 9070 XT بأسرع معمارية RDNA 4 بتصاميم تبريد متميزة من سافاير وجيجابايت وآسراك. من جانب إنتل، يبرز كرت Arc B570 بذاكرة 10 جيجابايت كأرخص كرت يستحق الشراء في 2026، بينما يأتي Arc B580 بذاكرة 12 جيجابايت مع مبرد سائل 360 مم ولعبتين مجاناً.

sections.heading: دليل المشتري: أربعة معايير حاسمة قبل اتخاذ القرار

paragraphs.text: ينصح الخبراء بتحديد دقة الشاشة وإعدادات الرسوم المستهدفة أولاً؛ فكروت الدخول تكفي لـ 1080p بإعدادات متوسطة، بينما تتطلب إعدادات ألترا وكروت 2K و 4K بطاقات أعلى. ثانياً، حدد معدل الإطارات المطلوب: 30 إطاراً للعبية، 60 إطاراً لتجربة جيدة، وأكثر من 100 إطار للألعاب التنافسية. ثالثاً، تحقق من قدرة مزود الطاقة باستخدام حاسبات متاحة مثل حاسبة نيوإيغ، ورابعاً، قارن أبعاد الكرت مع مساحة العلبة المتاحة، خاصة مع تصاميم التبريد ثلاثية المراوح الكبيرة.

تؤكد تومز هاردوير أن أفضل الصفقات تنفد بسرعة كبيرة، وأن القائمة تُحدث على مدار الساعة لتعكس أحدث الأسعار والتوفر. يُنصح بالعودة المتكررة للصفحة عند البحث عن كرت محدد، ومراجعة دليل أفضل كروت الشاشة للألعاب وقاعدة بيانات أداء الكروت لاتخاذ قرار مستنير بعيداً عن ضجيج العروض الموسمية.

ar.confidence_note: المقال مبني بالكامل على مصدر تومز هاردوير الأساسي مع التركيز على الحقائق التقنية والأسعار المعلنة، دون إضافة آراء شخصية أو معلومات غير موثقة.

en.title: Black Friday GPU Deals Focus on AMD and Intel Value
en.description: AMD and Intel graphics cards offer stronger value as AI demand, elevated prices and limited GPU supply reshape Black Friday 2026 gaming deals.
en.deck: Tom's Hardware says the 2026 Black Friday GPU market is defined less by traditional discounts and more by finding the lowest prices relative to unusually high current graphics-card costs.
summary_bullets: The global AI buildout is continuing to constrain consumer GPU supply and push prices higher.
Black Friday offers may provide relief, but near-MSRP pricing is largely absent in late 2026.
AMD and Intel cards currently offer better apparent value than many Nvidia-powered alternatives.
Budget, 1440p and 4K buyers have different options, while stock and coupons can change availability quickly.
en.confidence_note: High confidence for market conditions and model recommendations; pricing varies by retailer and was not stated in fixed dollar amounts.

sections.heading: AI demand keeps GPU prices elevated

paragraphs.text: The 2026 Black Friday gaming GPU market is developing under sustained pressure from the global AI buildout, according to [Tom's Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/gpus/best-gaming-graphics-card-gpu-deals-nvidia-amd-intel). The publication says demand for computing infrastructure linked to AI is constraining the supply available to consumer graphics-card buyers and contributing to steadily higher prices throughout the year.

In that environment, industry leaders cited in the report expect prices to continue rising. Finding a graphics card near its original MSRP has become increasingly uncommon. Instead, the Black Friday season is likely to offer a chance to buy at relatively low levels compared with elevated 2026 market prices rather than at prices seen in less constrained years.

Tom's Hardware advises shoppers who need an immediate upgrade to act when a genuinely strong option appears. It also frames Black Friday as a possible way to prepare for Grand Theft Auto VI's eventual PC release, while warning that some seemingly attractive cards have too weak a price-to-performance ratio to justify purchasing.

sections.heading: AMD and Intel cards lead the value list

paragraphs.text: The publication reports that it is seeing substantially better value from AMD and Intel cards than from Nvidia-powered models, although savings remain available for some RTX products. The recommendations are based on hands-on reviews, benchmarks and historical price analysis, and the list is being updated as supplies and promotions change.

At the budget end of the market, the Intel Arc B570 is presented as the cheapest graphics card worth buying in 2026. The ASRock model includes 10GB of VRAM and is described as particularly suitable for buyers prioritizing low cost. Tom's Hardware also highlights AMD's Radeon RX 9070 GRE, calling it strong for 1080p and 1440p gaming and especially attractive when an on-page coupon is applied.

The RX 9070 is positioned as a step up from the 9070 GRE, offering additional 1440p performance. Its 16GB frame buffer also gives it room to explore 4K gaming with upscaling. Because these cards are becoming scarce, the report urges interested buyers not to assume that listed availability will remain stable.

For buyers considering faster AMD hardware, the RX 9070 XT is described as AMD's most powerful RDNA 4 card. The ASRock Steel Legend model combines a triple-fan cooler with a white-and-silver design, while a Gigabyte option is identified as the cheapest 9070 XT listing then available. Both are presented as suitable for fast 1440p and 4K gaming.

sections.heading: Nvidia options span 1080p to enthusiast gaming

paragraphs.text: Nvidia remains represented across several [Black Friday](https://www.tomshardware.com/news/best-deals-on-tech) tiers, beginning with the GeForce RTX 5060. Tom's Hardware calls the 5060 efficient and a strong fit for 1080p gaming, particularly for its support for the full DLSS 4.5 feature set. The publication identifies one RTX 5060 model as having reached the lowest price it had seen during the Black Friday sales period.

The RTX 5060 Ti 8GB is recommended for buyers who want more performance than the 5060 without making a major jump in cost. It is described as capable in 1080p and 1440p raster gaming, with the cheapest examples selling near the same level as 5060 cards. Under those circumstances, Tom's Hardware argues that a buyer may be better served by the extra performance unless saving the final dollar is essential.

Higher up the stack, the triple-fan GeForce RTX 5070 is highlighted for 1440p raster and ray-tracing gaming, supported by DLSS upscaling and Multi Frame Generation. The RTX 5070 Ti is named as the publication's choice for an enthusiast graphics card across a broad range of gaming workloads, and an Asus model is described as the cheapest option available at the time.

The RTX 5090 remains highly unusual in this pricing environment. Tom's Hardware says there are no meaningful deals on the flagship, with one listed model costing more than three times MSRP. Even then, the report says that a 5090 purchase could make sense for someone who absolutely needs the card, particularly when it is bundled with a free motherboard.

sections.heading: What buyers should check before paying

paragraphs.text: A deal's quality depends heavily on the intended resolution and visual settings. Tom's Hardware says a low-end card can provide 1080p gaming at medium settings, while ultra settings generally require at least a mid-range GPU. More capable cards can target 2K and higher resolutions, with the priciest models intended for 4K performance.

Frame rate expectations are another practical factor. The publication says 30 fps is widely considered the minimum for playability and 60 fps a reasonable target. Competitive esports players seeking less lag may need more than 100 fps at practical settings, making benchmark performance more useful than a headline discount.

Before completing a purchase, buyers should confirm that their power supply has enough capacity and that the new card physically fits in the PC case. The report also recommends checking current GPU benchmarks and targeted buying advice rather than relying solely on a temporary coupon or limited-time offer.

sections.heading: Availability may be as important as the discount

paragraphs.text: Stock remains a central risk. The strongest offers can sell out quickly, and the Tom's Hardware list is being updated around the clock with changing prices and availability. Buyers may therefore need to judge a deal promptly rather than waiting for a later promotion that could disappear or prove less competitive.

Several featured cards have additional conditions attached to their best prices, including on-page retailer coupons. In some cases, bundles add further value, such as a free motherboard with the RTX 5090 or a promotional AIO cooler with selected AMD or Intel purchases. Those extras do not change a graphics card's baseline performance, but they can affect whether the overall package is worthwhile.

The overall message is restrained: Black Friday 2026 may produce the lowest current market prices for many gaming GPUs, but it does not necessarily restore affordability or normal MSRP pricing. The strongest recommendations remain concentrated on cards that balance resolution, performance and long-term usefulness, rather than on every visible discount.
